prompt: I'm building a new SaaS backend with Express and TypeScript. I need to set up the project structure, and the API has resources for teams, projects, and tasks with nested routes. Each team has members with different roles (admin, editor, viewer). I need a typed error system that gives the frontend consistent error shapes including validation errors with field-level detail. Scaffold the project structure, the router hierarchy, and the error classes.

assertions.name: feature-first structure
assertions.description: Uses feature-first organization (not layer-first)

assertions.name: typed error hierarchy
assertions.description: Defines typed error classes (not generic Error)

assertions.name: validation error with field details
assertions.description: Validation errors include field-level detail

assertions.name: three-layer separation
assertions.description: Controller-service-repository layers are separated

assertions.name: global error handler
assertions.description: Has a global error handler middleware

prompt: I need to add JWT authentication to an existing Next.js app that has an Express backend. The frontend should store the access token in memory and use an httpOnly cookie for the refresh token. I need the middleware chain set up correctly (request ID -> logging -> CORS -> rate limit -> auth -> validation -> handler -> error handler), and the frontend needs to intercept 401 responses to transparently refresh the token and retry the request. Show me both the backend middleware and the frontend API client.

assertions.name: correct middleware order
assertions.description: Middleware chain follows the documented order

assertions.name: httpOnly refresh cookie
assertions.description: Refresh token uses httpOnly cookie, not localStorage

assertions.name: transparent 401 retry
assertions.description: Frontend intercepts 401, refreshes token, retries

assertions.name: JWT short expiry
assertions.description: Access token has short expiry (15min or less)

assertions.name: RBAC or authz check
assertions.description: Includes role-based or permission-based authorization

prompt: I have a working FastAPI backend for an e-commerce app, but it's not production-ready. I need health check endpoints, graceful shutdown, CORS with explicit origins, structured JSON logging with request IDs, and a global error handler that returns consistent JSON error responses. The app uses PostgreSQL with async queries and Redis for caching. Walk me through the production hardening checklist and show me the patterns for each item.

assertions.name: health check endpoints
assertions.description: Creates /health and /ready endpoints

assertions.name: graceful shutdown
assertions.description: Implements SIGTERM handler with drain + cleanup

assertions.name: structured JSON logging
assertions.description: Uses structured JSON logs with request IDs

assertions.name: global error handler
assertions.description: Returns consistent JSON error shape

assertions.name: CORS explicit origins
assertions.description: CORS configured with explicit origins, not wildcard

prompt: I'm building a simple weather API in Express that just serves public forecast data. No authentication needed. Just give me the project structure, error handling, and a health check endpoint. I want to keep it minimal but well-organized. The API has a single resource (forecasts) with GET endpoints and a periodic background job that refreshes the data from an external weather service.

assertions.name: no auth middleware forced
assertions.description: Does not force authentication where none is needed

assertions.name: minimal structure
assertions.description: Provides lean structure appropriate to API complexity

assertions.name: background job pattern
assertions.description: Includes idempotent background job pattern for data refresh

assertions.name: error handling present
assertions.description: Includes typed errors and global handler even for simple API

prompt: I have a GraphQL API built with a Rust backend (Actix-web + async-graphql) and a Svelte frontend. The API handles file uploads for a photo gallery, needs real-time subscription updates when new photos are added, and uses PostgreSQL with connection pooling. Show me the fullstack integration patterns — especially the subscription setup on both sides, the file upload flow with presigned URLs, and how to share types between the Rust backend and Svelte frontend.

assertions.name: acknowledges Rust gap
assertions.description: Notes that Rust rules don't exist and points to external references

assertions.name: real-time subscription pattern
assertions.description: Provides GraphQL subscription setup for both server and client

assertions.name: presigned URL upload
assertions.description: Recommends presigned URL pattern for photo uploads

assertions.name: type sharing strategy
assertions.description: Addresses type sharing between Rust and Svelte

assertions.name: handles instead of avoids
assertions.description: Does not bail out — provides useful patterns despite unknown stack

prompt: I'm breaking a monolithic e-commerce API into microservices (orders, inventory, payments). Each service needs its own Express app, database (PostgreSQL), and deployment. Services communicate via RabbitMQ for events (order.placed, inventory.reserved, payment.completed) and need a saga pattern for the checkout flow. I also need an API gateway that handles auth and routes requests to the correct service. Show me the project structure, the inter-service event contracts, the saga orchestrator, and how each service maintains its own three-layer separation.

assertions.name: per-service feature-first
assertions.description: Each microservice maintains feature-first organization

assertions.name: typed event contracts
assertions.description: Inter-service events are typed and versioned

assertions.name: saga pattern for checkout
assertions.description: Compensating transactions on failure via saga orchestrator

assertions.name: shared auth across services
assertions.description: API gateway handles auth, services trust internal token

assertions.name: independent three-layer separation
assertions.description: Each service has its own controller/service/repository layers

prompt: I'm building a task management app that needs to work offline. The frontend is a React PWA and the backend is Express with PostgreSQL. When offline, users should still be able to create and edit tasks, and changes should sync when connectivity returns. I need conflict resolution for edits made while offline. Show me the service worker setup, the IndexedDB schema, the sync queue with retry logic, and the backend conflict resolution strategy.

assertions.name: service worker with cache
assertions.description: Registers service worker and caches app shell + API responses

assertions.name: IndexedDB local store
assertions.description: Offline writes go to IndexedDB before attempting API call

assertions.name: sync queue with retry
assertions.description: Queues offline mutations, replays when connectivity returns

assertions.name: conflict resolution strategy
assertions.description: Backend resolves conflicts (last-write-wins or version vectors)

assertions.name: auth survives offline
assertions.description: Auth token state preserved across offline/online cycles

prompt: I'm designing a notification system for a SaaS platform. Events are produced by various services (user.signup, order.placed, payment.received, invoice.generated) and consumed by a notification service that sends emails, push notifications, and in-app alerts. I need the outbox pattern to guarantee delivery, idempotent consumers, and a dead letter queue for failed deliveries. Show me the event schema design with versioning, the outbox pattern implementation with the same DB transaction, the consumer idempotency key tracking, and the DLQ with retry count.

assertions.name: outbox pattern
assertions.description: Events written to outbox table in same DB transaction as business operation

assertions.name: idempotent consumers
assertions.description: Consumer tracks processed event IDs to prevent duplicates

assertions.name: dead letter queue
assertions.description: Failed events routed to DLQ with retry count tracking

assertions.name: event schema versioning
assertions.description: Events carry a version field for schema evolution

assertions.name: consistent error handling
assertions.description: Typed errors and structured logging across all producers/consumers

prompt: My Next.js app is failing to build with a cryptic webpack error. I've tried clearing node_modules and reinstalling but it still fails. The error message mentions something about module resolution and a missing dependency in my API route. Can you help me debug this build failure and get my app running again?

assertions.name: recognizes out-of-scope
assertions.description: Identifies this as a build failure diagnosis (not a fullstack architecture task)

assertions.name: redirects to build-resolver
assertions.description: States that this should be handled by build-resolver skill

assertions.name: does not attempt full diagnosis
assertions.description: Does not provide step-by-step debugging of the build error

assertions.name: offers useful boundary info
assertions.description: Provides relevant context the user should share with build-resolver

prompt: I'm building a cross-platform mobile app with a Swift iOS client, a Kotlin Android client, and a Go backend. The backend uses gRPC for inter-service communication and exposes a REST API for mobile clients. I need push notifications, offline data sync with CRDT-based conflict resolution, and OAuth2 with Google and Apple Sign-In. There's no database yet — I'm deciding between CockroachDB and DynamoDB. Show me the full architecture, the project structure for all three platforms, how auth flows work end-to-end, and how offline sync resolves conflicts.

assertions.name: acknowledges platform gaps
assertions.description: States that no language rules exist for Swift, Kotlin, or Go

assertions.name: references external sources
assertions.description: Points to external style guides for Swift, Kotlin, and Go

assertions.name: applies architecture patterns
assertions.description: Still applies feature-first, error handling, config patterns where applicable

assertions.name: addresses DB decision
assertions.description: Provides reasoned recommendation on CockroachDB vs DynamoDB

assertions.name: does not bail out
assertions.description: Provides useful architecture guidance despite unknown stacks
